scope: Issue 31 final extension; candidate dispositions are separate from implementation/verification status.

candidates.problem: Model-specific edits are interleaved with shared row work.
candidates.contract: Separate full mutable/immutable/insert-only lifecycles and separate metadata owners; top-level Run remains common.
candidates.sufficiency: Current shared first insertion, duplicate and metadata obligations make this particular broad ownership split costlier without a present independent lifecycle requirement.
candidates.unmeasured: No implementation or developer-time benchmark; not needed to identify this candidate's distributed shared obligations.
candidates.reopenCondition: An approved model change makes work/admission/metadata semantics independently necessary, or a concrete revised contract removes distributed shared ownership. A narrow common-orchestrator seam is a different candidate.

candidates.problem: Local mutable/immutable stored-operation validation changes may require inspecting unrelated row work.
candidates.contract: A2: one internal module for mutable UPDATE/DELETE and immutable Red execution/receipt validation, caller owns no-op, comparison, Work, retirement, Lineage, common Black, Processing and Run. B2 variant: only mutable DML in a private same-file function. Neither is broad fragmentation.
candidates.sufficiency: Enough to specify behavior and a feasible comparison; not enough to decide net maintenance benefit of either seam. Their unchanged caller guards/flags and new interface may offset local focus.

missingContext.question: For the stated seam, does one real locator or malformed-return change/reproduction remove unrelated implementation/fixture obligations without expanding the interface or moving prerequisite timing?
missingContext.attempt: Retrieved current body, model history, stable-identity Decision and malformed-return/fault tests. These establish the task and constraints but compare neither proposed seam against keep.
missingContext.smallestNextObservation: Review-only interface/body sketch and replay of one existing mutable locator/returned-key task on B2 and that exact candidate; record touched units, inputs, caller facts, fixture capabilities, ordered effects and unchanged gates.
missingContext.supplier: Implementation/review agent; no new business decision required.

candidates.reopenCondition: New evidence specifically addresses M1: a completed scoped comparison, or a concrete mutable/Red validation change or incident demonstrating unrelated caller/fixture burden. Path/keyword match alone is insufficient; new task evidence reopens evaluation, not automatic ADOPT.
candidates.remainingAfterReopen: Safety/meaning checks remain; historical correctness coverage or a green CI alone does not answer M1.

candidates.problem: Two row-mode branches maintain the same release/delete/exactly-one retirement obligation.
candidates.contract: Private same-file retireRowActive(query, activeId, linkId); only fixed release SQL, delete SQL, exactly-one result. Caller retains routine branch and Lineage; no transactions or model decisions.
candidates.sufficiency: The identical FK-sensitive protocol has two source owners; a three-input helper replaces one duplicate without changing SQL/ordering. Source-level benefit and cost support adoption, separately from gates.
candidates.reopenCondition: The two call sites need different retirement order/cardinality, helper inputs grow into mutable context, or traces/regressions differ.

candidates.problem: Rule v2 groups speculative evidence and sufficient cost objections into Keep, losing the distinction exposed by the model question.
candidates.contract: One canonical rule for ADOPT/REJECT/DEFER, candidate-specific retrieval and missing/reopen evidence, short existing AGENTS/Decision pointers.
candidates.sufficiency: Actual rule text and prior insufficient candidate comparison establish the ambiguity; no runtime metric is required to distinguish knowledge states.
candidates.reopenCondition: Normal use produces gratuitous records, fails to distinguish labels or treats a touched path as sufficient new evidence.
